title: Regional fleet runway, SKU mix, and reorder schedule
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational sheet for regional GPU fleet runway and recommended reorder schedule by SKU. Intended for infra PM + procurement to use as a short-lived working reference and to feed monthly PO queuing. Replace with canonical spreadsheet when order commitments are finalized.

Summary (top line):
We currently have ~18 weeks of net runway across global fleet given current burn and reserved commitments. APAC is the most constrained (8–10w) and needs an immediate partial hedge of 3–5 H100 equivalents to avoid degraded SLAs on Dedicated. This doc shows per-SKU reorder points, lead-time assumptions, and a staggered order calendar to smooth deliveries.

Assumptions and definitions:
- Daily burn = average GPU-hours consumed per day normalized to 1-GPU 1x utilization baseline.
- Reserved backs = committed reserved capacity (dedicated customers) that cannot be preempted.
- Day-of-runway = (inventory - reserved backs) / daily burn.
- Safety stock target = max(10% of 12w burn, lead_time_variance * daily_burn).

Current inventory snapshot (as-of 2024-09-10):
Region | SKU | Units on-hand | Reserved units | Weekly burn (units/week) | Days-of-runway (approx)
US-West | H100-80GB | 120 | 70 | 36 | 28
US-East | A100-80GB | 200 | 90 | 40 | 46
EU (Frankfurt) | H100-80GB | 40 | 25 | 30 | 9
APAC (SG) | H100-80GB | 22 | 18 | 34 | 6
APAC (Tokyo) | L40 | 45 | 10 | 8 | 42
US-West | A10 | 80 | 5 | 5 | 112
Notes: days-of-runway computed as (on-hand - reserved)/daily_burn * 7 for weekly burn. Numbers rounded for quick planning.

Vendor lead-time matrix (vendor-level historical median and variance):
Vendor | SKU families | Typical lead (weeks) | 90th pctile lead (weeks) | Notes
Vendor-A (authorized) | H100 / A100 family | 10–14 | 18 | shipping + customs delays APAC
Vendor-B (broker) | H100 / specialty | 6–10 | 12 | faster for spot buys, higher price
Vendor-C (OEM resell) | L40 / A10 / T4 | 4–8 | 10 | good for non-cutting edge SKUs
Cloud-burst lease | Any | 0–2 | 4 | Expensive but immediate for bursts

Reorder-point calculations (example listing):
Formula: reorder_point_units = daily_burn * lead_time_days + safety_stock_units
Examples using current weekly burn converted to daily burn (week/7):
- EU H100: daily_burn = 30/7 ~ 4.3, lead_time = 12w ~ 84 days -> rp = 4.3*84 + safety(≈27) => rp ≈ 360 units (high-level, indicates we need bulk ordering if we want to fully cover long lead).
- APAC H100: with current on-hand 22 and reserved 18 -> usable = 4 units. To hit a 12w hedge we'd need ~4.3*84 ≈ 360 as above; unrealistic to full fill immediately. Tactical recommendation below.

Tactical procurement schedule (recommended 12-week cadence, prioritize through week buckets):
- Week 0–4: Immediate broker orders for APAC: 3 H100 equivalents via Vendor-B (6–8 week lead expected) + 6 L40 to cover moderate inference class. Raise POs and flag for express shipment if arrival slips past week 8.
- Week 4–8: Place primary Vendor-A order for 50 H100s split US/ EU (10–14w lead) to arrive around weeks 14–18. Negotiate partial shipments (25/25) to fall into week 12 and week 16 windows.
- Week 8–12: Supplemental A100 batch (60 units) to US-East to relieve A100 pressure and enable some workload consolidation from H100 where possible.
- Contingency: confirm 200-GPU short-term leasing line with cloud-burst partner (expires 2025-01) to provide immediate headroom if any shipment delays push us under 4w runway in any region.

SKU mix guidance (workload-matching + cost per token heuristics):
- H100: primary for high-throughput model serving (LLM decoder workloads). Prioritize H100 in regions with heavy Dedicated commitments.
- A100: best price/perf for older LLM families and for mixed inference. Use A100 to fill base capacity in US-East.
- L40/A10: inference and small-model embedding fleets — useful as cheaper overflow for low-latency endpoints.
Strategy: target ~55% H100 family (global effective capacity), 30% A100 family, 15% L40/A10/T4. This is adjustable by expected mix of embeddings vs generation workloads.

Staggering and arrival smoothing rules (to avoid single-window capacity shocks):
- No single PO should exceed 25% of region total needed for next 36 weeks unless price delta > 15% or vendor requires minimums.
- Prefer partial-shipment clauses in all Vendor-A contracts. Insert liquidated-damages SLA for >4 week slip on scheduled partial.
- Reserve 10% of weekly freight capacity (crates/warehousing) for overflow to prevent arrival backlog.

Contingency playbook (when runway < 6 weeks):
- Immediate: enable cross-region spill (route up to 20% of Dedicated traffic to underutilized region) and activate cloud-burst leasing for hot services.
- 24–72h: pause non-critical batch training, escalate POs to express shipping, and call Vendor-B broker queue.
- 1–3 weeks: execute emergency lease + prioritize customer notifications for affected SLAs if mitigation insufficient.

Open questions / decisions needed (short list):
- Procurement: can we push for 25% partial shipments with Vendor-A on the next RFP? (Procurement lead: Priya)
- Finance: confirm acceptable forward-commitment discount threshold for 12–24 month reservation (currently quoted 8–12% discount).
- Legal: standardize customs tax allocation for APAC deliveries to avoid 2–3w deterministic delays.

Action items / owners (next 7 days):
- Priya: issue broker POs for 3 H100 equiv and 6 L40 to Vendor-B by 2024-09-18.
- Diego: validate leasing partner terms + update contract (due 2024-09-20).
- Maya: produce a PO queue spreadsheet (canonical) and set recurring weekly sync with procurement (calendar invite sent).
- Ethan: model cost impact of partial shipments vs single-batch discount and share by 2024-09-22 (GH: repo infra-capacity/cost-model).

Notes to self / working thoughts (informal):
- APAC customs has been our wild card; allow +2w buffer by default for SG->JP shipments.
- Might be worth engaging a freight forwarder (3rd party) solely for H100 shipments to APAC to reduce variance.
- Consider converting some Reserved backfills to A100 to free H100 for latency-sensitive Dedicated routes (requires ops migration effort).

Appendix — quick calcs and shorthand: 
- Global weekly burn (approx): 160 units/week -> daily ~23 units/day.
- Safety stock default: max(10% of 12w burn=0.1*(160*12)=192) vs lead variance*daily -> keep safety = 192 units global as rough anchor.
- Quick reorder heuristic: if region_days_of_runway <= 12 -> escalate to broker/lease immediately.
